# Data
**MTA Data**
```{r}
project <- read.csv("~/Desktop/Fall 2026/DATS6101/DATS6101_Project_MTA_Subway_Hourly_Ridership.csv")
# project <- read.csv("~/Desktop/Cloning-Git/DATS6101-project1/DATS6101_Project_MTA_Subway_Hourly_Ridership.csv")
```

```{r}
# Make sure columns are cast to correct types
project$borough <- as.factor(project$borough)
project$payment_method <- as.factor(project$payment_method)
project$fare_class_category <- as.factor(project$fare_class_category)
project$ridership <- as.numeric(gsub(",", "", project$ridership))
project$transfers <- as.numeric(gsub(",", "", project$transfers))

## Created Variables of Analysis
# Add 24-hour time column
project <- project %>%
  mutate(
    timestamp = mdy_hms(transit_timestamp),
    hour = hour(timestamp)
  )

# Add categories for morning, afternoon, evening, night
# Morning (5am - 10:59am), afternoon (11am - 3:59pm), evening (4pm - 8:59pm), night (9pm - 4:59am)
project <- project %>%
  mutate(
    time_of_day = case_when(
      hour >= 5 & hour < 11 ~ "Morning",
      hour >= 11 & hour < 16 ~ "Mid Day",
      hour >= 16 & hour < 21 ~ "Evening",
      TRUE ~ "Night"
    )
  )

# Add day of week column
project <- project %>%
  mutate(
    day_of_week = wday(timestamp, label = TRUE)
  )

# Weekend vs. Weekday column
project <- project %>%
  mutate(day_type = if_else(day_of_week %in% c("Sat", "Sun"), "Weekend", "Weekday"))

# Commuter hours column
project <- project %>%
  mutate(
    commute_type = case_when(
      day_type == "Weekday" & hour >= 5 & hour < 11 ~ "Morning Commute",
      day_type == "Weekday" & hour >= 16 & hour < 21 ~ "Evening Commute",
      TRUE ~ "Other Hours"
    )
  )

project$time_of_day <- as.factor(project$time_of_day)
project$day_of_week <- as.factor(project$day_of_week)
project$day_type <- as.factor(project$day_type)
project$commute_type <- as.factor(project$commute_type)
```

```{r}
# Our chosen census variables for the model
census_variables <- c(
  population = "B01003_001",
  median_income = "B19013_001"
)

nyc_counties <- c(
  "Bronx", # The Bronx
  "Kings", # Brooklyn
  "New York", # Manhattan
  "Queens" # Queens
)
```

```{r}
nyc_census <- map_dfr(
  nyc_counties, ~ get_acs(
    geography = "tract",
    variables = census_variables,
    state = "NY",
    county = .x,
    year = 2024,
    survey = "acs5",
    output = "wide",
    geometry = TRUE
  )
)
```

**Joining Data**
```{r}
# Read in NYC neighborhood data
neighborhoods <- read.csv("~/Desktop/Fall 2026/DATS6101/2020_Census_Tracts.csv")

# Clean the data for joining
neighborhoods <- neighborhoods %>%
  mutate(GEOID = as.character(GEOID)) %>%
  select(GEOID, NTACode, NTAName)
```

```{r}
# Join neighborhood names to the census tracts using GEOID
nyc_census <- nyc_census %>%
  left_join(neighborhoods, by = "GEOID")
```

```{r}
# Create one representative set of coordinates for each station complex
stations <- project %>%
  distinct(station_complex_id, station_complex, borough, latitude, longitude) %>%
  group_by(station_complex_id, station_complex, borough) %>%
  summarize(latitude = mean(latitude, na.rm = TRUE), longitude = mean(longitude, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
# Convert the stations into spatial points, and make sure census data uses the same coordinate system
stations_sf <- st_as_sf(
  stations,
  coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
  crs = 4326,
  remove = FALSE
)

nyc_census <- st_transform(
  nyc_census,
  crs = 4326
)
```

```{r}
# Spatial join: match each station to the census tract containing its coordinates
stations_census <- st_join(
  stations_sf,
  nyc_census,
  join = st_within,
  left = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
# Mapping census and neighborhood data to MTA stations 
station_info <- stations_census %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(
    station_complex_id,
    GEOID,
    NTACode,
    NTAName,
    populationE,
    median_incomeE
  )
```

```{r}
# Final join
project <- project %>%
  left_join(
    station_info,
    by = "station_complex_id"
  )
```

Join the Census tracts to corresponding neighborhoods using GEOID
Create one specific location point for each station
Spatially match each station to the Census tract
Join population, income, and neighborhood to each tract
Join the results back to MTA data by station ID

Each row in `project` represents the original project 1 data, with:
- Associated neighborhood (NTA) of that station based on coordinated
- Associated Census statistics for the tract that the station is in (based on location)
